content: 1. Atazanavir and Desogestrel: Atazanavir can either increase or decrease the levels of desogestrel by affecting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 2. Cobicistat and Dexlansoprazole: Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Atazanavir and Desvenlafaxine: Atazanavir increases desvenlafaxine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Atazanavir and Dexamethasone: Atazanavir increases dexamethasone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Atazanavir and Diazepam: Atazanavir increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase toxicity. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 6. Cobicistat and Diazepam: Cobicistat increases diazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and a reduced diazepam dose may be required. 7. Cobicistat and Diazepam Buccal: Cobicistat increases diazepam buccal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Atazanavir and Diazepam Buccal: Atazanavir increases diazepam buccal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Cobicistat and Diazepam Intranasal: Cobicistat increases diazepam intranasal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Atazanavir and Diazepam Intranasal: Atazanavir increases diazepam intranasal levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Atazanavir and Diazoxide: Atazanavir increases the effects of diazoxide, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Digoxin: Cobicistat increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 13. Atazanavir and Diclofenac: Atazanavir increases diclofenac levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Didanosine and Atazanavir: Didanosine decreases atazanavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Atazanavir and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 16. Atazanavir and Digoxin: Atazanavir increases digoxin levels through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of atrioventricular (AV) block. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Atazanavir and Diltiazem: Atazanavir increases diltiazem levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing toxicities such as hypotension and AV block. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and the diltiazem dose should be reduced by 50%. 18. Cobicistat and Diltiazem: Cobicistat increases diltiazem levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Cobicistat and Disopyramide: Cobicistat increases disopyramide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. 20. Atazanavir and Dofetilide: Atazanavir increases dofetilide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 21. Cobicistat and Docetaxel: Cobicistat increases docetaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored, and a 50% reduction in docetaxel dosing may be considered if coadministration cannot be avoided. 22. Atazanavir and Dolasetron: Atazanavir increases dolasetron levels, potentially increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 23. Cobicistat and Doravirine: Cobicistat increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Atazanavir and Doravirine: Atazanavir increases doravirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Atazanavir and Dosulepin: Atazanavir increases dosulepin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cobicistat and Doxepin: Cobicistat increases doxepin levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor its response during coadministration. 27. Atazanavir and Doxepin: Atazanavir increases doxepin levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Atazanavir and Doxorubicin: Atazanavir increases doxorubicin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cobicistat and Dronabinol: Cobicistat increases dronabinol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Atazanavir and Dronabinol: Atazanavir increases dronabinol levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Atazanavir and Drospirenone: Atazanavir may increase or decrease drospirenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Alternatives should be considered if available. 32. Atazanavir and Duvelisib: Atazanavir increases duvelisib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of duvelisib toxicities. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 33. Cobicistat and Efavirenz: Cobicistat increases efavirenz levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Atazanavir and Efavirenz: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Cobicistat and Elagolix: Cobicistat increases elagolix levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 36. Atazanavir and Elagolix: Atazanavir increases elagolix levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 37. Cobicistat and Elvitegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Cobicistat increases the levels of this combination therapy by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Atazanavir and Elvitegravir: Atazanavir significantly increases elvitegravir levels. There are no data available to alter current dosing recommendations. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Atazanavir and Emtricitabine: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cobicistat and Encorafenib: Cobicistat increases encorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Atazanavir and Encorafenib: Atazanavir increases encorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Atazanavir and Enfortumab Vedotin: Atazanavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat and Enfortumab Vedotin: Cobicistat increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Atazanavir and Enfuvirtide: Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Enzalutamide and Cobicistat: Enzalutamide decreases cobicistat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Atazanavir and Erlotinib: Atazanavir increases erlotinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 47. Cobicistat and Erlotinib: Cobicistat increases erlotinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 48. Erythromycin and Atazanavir: Erythromycin increases atazanavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat and Escitalopram: Cobicistat increases escitalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Atazanavir and Escitalopram: Atazanavir increases escitalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of serotonin syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely.
